terms.definition: An error that makes repeat readings scatter unpredictably about the true value.
terms.examiner: Reduced by repeating and averaging; it affects precision, not accuracy.

terms.definition: An error that shifts every reading by the same amount or in the same direction, such as a zero error.
terms.examiner: Repeating does not remove it. Check zero readings and calibrate the instrument.

terms.definition: How close repeat measurements are to each other (how little they scatter).
terms.examiner: Do not confuse with accuracy. A precise set can still be inaccurate.

terms.definition: How close a measurement is to the true value.
terms.examiner: Mark schemes reject 'accurate' used to mean 'precise'.

terms.definition: The same results are obtained when the original experimenter repeats the experiment with the same method and equipment.
terms.examiner: Contrast with reproducibility (a different person or method).

terms.definition: The smallest change in the quantity being measured that gives a recognisable change in the reading.
terms.examiner: A metre rule has a resolution of 1 mm; uncertainty is often taken as the resolution or half of it.
Add percentage uncertainties for products and quotients; double it for a squared quantity.
